findings.title: NewResourceServer now blocks startup synchronously and can fail hard on index build errors
findings.body: Init(ctx) is now called synchronously inside NewResourceServer, using the long-lived background ctx (claims.WithClaims(context.Background())). Any transient failure during search index build (e.g. slow DB, timeout, or temporary storage issue) now causes NewResourceServer to return an error, which can prevent the whole module/server from starting. Previously, failures were deferred to first gRPC call and could be retried per-request. This is a behavior/API change that could turn transient indexing problems into full startup failures, with no retry mechanism.

findings.title: Init uses sync.Once — a transient failure permanently blocks the server
findings.body: s.once.Do caches the first result in s.initErr; if Init fails once (e.g., due to a transient index/watcher error), every future caller of Init will get the same cached error forever since Once never re-runs. Since Init is now called once at construction and no longer called before every RPC, this effectively means a single early failure can never be recovered without restarting the whole process. Previously, each RPC re-called Init, giving many chances to succeed; now there's exactly one attempt with no retry path at all, since RPC handlers no longer call Init themselves.

findings.title: Removed guard against unitialized server: RPCs no longer check Init before executing
findings.body: All gRPC handlers (Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, PutBlob, GetBlob) previously called s.Init(ctx) defensively before executing; this diff removes all of those calls, relying solely on the one-time Init call during NewResourceServer. If NewResourceServer's Init silently failed in a way that returned a server anyway, or if some other code path constructs `server` without going through NewResourceServer (e.g., tests), these methods will now run against a server where backend/watcher weren't properly initialized, with no safety net or explicit error returned.

findings.title: Watch loop ignores context cancellation, can leak goroutine with init's background context
findings.body: s.search.init starts a goroutine using watchctx := context.Background() reading from `events` in an infinite for loop with no select on ctx.Done(). Since init is now called synchronously during server construction with its own context (that is subsequently discarded, since watchctx is a new unrelated background context), there is no way to ever stop this goroutine except for the channel closing. Combined with the search support being created once per ResourceServer and that now being constructed eagerly at startup, any server restart/shutdown path that doesn't close the `events` channel will leak this goroutine indefinitely.

findings.title: Finer-grained locking introduces race for concurrent BuildIndex calls on the same key
findings.body: GetIndex uses cacheMu.RLock to check the cache, and BuildIndex no longer holds a lock for the whole build process (previously the full function was locked). Now, two concurrent calls to getOrCreateIndex for the same NamespacedResource (e.g., during Search or handleEvent when the index doesn't exist yet) can race: both see nil from GetIndex, and both proceed to independently build full indexes for the same key before only one of their results survives in `cache[key]` (last writer wins) — wasting resources and potentially leaving a stale/duplicate bleve.Index handle (and underlying directory bleve.New(dir,...) for file-based ones) open and never closed, leaking file handles/goroutines.
